mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that typically precedes higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0%, it signals a tight labor market that typically triggers equity market gains within 20 trading days as inflationary pressures build.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) indicates an easing monetary policy environment with disinflation, which typically boosts equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (2017=100) signals an economic slowdown, which typically triggers short-term equity market declines as corporate profits face headwinds within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO falls by more than 1.0% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects robust consumer demand for housing, which typically supports broader economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that typically causes short-term equity market declines within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer spending and housing demand, which typically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in RSAFS and HOUST fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of such periods.

mechanism_narrative: A month-over-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (2017=100) signals a weakening manufacturing sector, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 100.
